Alesund is a major cruise port and one of Norway's most picturesque fishing towns. It is located at the mouth of Stor Fjord and is actually on two islands connected by bridges. Cruise ships dock close to downtown, so shopping and city touring can be done on foot.

Alesund is one of the "Express Route" ferry ports visited regularly as part of the government-subsidized passenger and cargo shipping service in Norway. The cruiseferry itinerary is between two homeports - Bergen (southmost) and Kirkenes (northmost) and connects a total of 34 ports, which are Norwegian communities without any road or air access. Independant tour operators offer from Alesund guided tours to Hjorundfjorden.

In June 2022, Enova SF (Norwegian state-owned enterprise) provided grants for installing shore power connectivity at several Norwegian cruise ports (including Alesund), scheduled for completion and inauguration in 2023. Between 2016-2022, Enova granted a total of NOK 842 million for 119 such projects. The technology allows the berthed cruise ship to shut down its diesel engines and instead use the city-grid electricity for the onboard hotel operations and services, thus saving fuel and reducing emissions. Enova SF (2001-founded government enterprise) is owned by Norway's Ministry of Petroleum and Energy and managed by the Ministry of Climate and Environment.

From Alesund, cruise tourists can take the 400 steps up to Kniven Overlook (Mt Aksla) for a spectacular panoramic view of the bay surrounded by offshore islands and mountains. The town was rebuilt with stone (instead of wood) following a devastating fire in 1904. The modern city is rich in art nouveau architecture (turrets, towers, medieval facades).

Further out is the outdoor Sunnmore Museum where guests can see a collection of boats and traditional farmhouses and the Medieval Museum which features a recreation of a 10th-century village. The Atlantic Ocean Marine Park is also on the outskirts with massive seascape tanks created into the coastline. Cruisers can also visit the Giske islands (burial mounds) and Godoy (lighthouse).

Alesund is a starting point for touring the hills of the Sunnmore region, Norang Valley, Oye Glaciers, Runde Island. As a settlement, Alesund was established in the 9th century when the Viking Rollo/Rolf (850-930/Normandy's first ruler between 911-928) built a castle nearby. The village received town status in 1848.

Alesund cruise terminal

Alesund is one of the ferry ports along the "Express Route" - Norway's Government subsidized "Norwegian Coastal Express". This is a regularly scheduled passenger and cargo shipping service in Norway. The "ferry and cruise" itinerary is between two turnaround ports - Bergen (southmost) and Kirkenes (northmost). It connects a total of 34 ports, which are Norwegian communities without any road or air access.

Since January 2021, Norway's coastal ferry service is operated by two companies - Hurtigruten (7 ships) and Havila (4 ships). The Norwegian Government's annual subsidy for the ferry service is around USD 100 million.

The list of all ports along the northbound "Norwegian Coastal Express" itinerary includes Bergen (turnaround port), Alesund, Floro, Geiranger (Stranda), Maloy (Vagsoy), Molde, Torvik (Heroy, Leinoya Island), Kristiansund, Rorvik (Vikna), Trondheim, Bodo, Bronnoysund (Bronnoy), Nesna, Ornes (Meloy), Sandnessjoen (Alstahaug), Stamsund (Vestvagoy Island), Svolvaer (Vagan, Austvagoya Island), Trollfjorden (Hadsel), Finnsnes (Lenvik), Harstad (Hinnoya Island), Risoyhamn (Andoy Island), Skjervoy, Sortland (Langoya Island), Stokmarknes (Hadseloya Island), Tromso, Berlevag, Hammerfest, Honningsvag (Mageroya Island, Nordkapp / North Cape), Kjollefjord (Lebesby), Mehamn (Gamvik), Oksfjord (Loppa), Batsfjord, Vardo (Vardoya Island), Kirkenes (turnaround port).

Ålesund is one of the easiest Norwegian cruise ports to explore independently. Ships normally berth directly beside the compact city centre, putting the Art Nouveau district, Brosundet waterfront and the foot of Mount Aksla within walking distance. A cruise call can therefore work well without an organized excursion, while taxis, local buses and cruise-day sightseeing services make the aquarium and surrounding islands practical alternatives.

At a Glance

  • Independent sightseeing: Easy independently.
  • Port access: Cruise ships normally dock rather than tender.
  • Main berths: The central Sørsidekaiene cruise area includes Storneskaia, Stornespiren and Prestebrygga. Berth assignments can change, particularly when several ships are in port.
  • Walking: Excellent for the central sights. Some streets are cobbled or sloping, and Mount Aksla requires a substantial stair climb if approached on foot.
  • Best for a short call: Brosundet, the Art Nouveau streets and Mount Aksla.

Getting from the Cruise Port

The main cruise berths are immediately beside central Ålesund. Passengers can normally leave the secure quay area and continue into town on foot without a shuttle transfer. Brosundet, Jugendstilsenteret, Ålesund Church and the entrance to the Mount Aksla steps can generally be reached within about 20 minutes from the ship.

Port security fencing may alter the exact pedestrian exit when ships are alongside, and parts of the quay or the movable bridge at Brosundet can be closed during cruise operations. Follow the signed passenger route rather than assuming the shortest route visible from the ship is open.

Local FRAM buses serve destinations outside the centre. Cruise-day sightseeing buses and the Ålesund city train also operate seasonally; the city train makes a circuit of about 70 minutes including a stop at the Fjellstua viewpoint. Taxis are normally available around cruise calls.

Best Ways to Spend Your Time

Art Nouveau Centre, Brosundet and Mount Aksla

Allow about 2.5–4 hours. This is the most practical first visit and requires no transport. Walk through the Art Nouveau centre, cross Hellebroa for views along Brosundet, and visit Jugendstilsenteret if you want more context on the rebuilding of Ålesund after the 1904 fire.

Continue to Byparken and climb the 418 steps to Fjellstua on Mount Aksla. The climb is steep, with viewpoints along the way, and the tourist office recommends allowing roughly 30–40 minutes for the journey uphill on foot. Passengers who do not want the stair climb can use a taxi or a sightseeing service that drives to the upper viewpoint.

Atlanterhavsparken Aquarium

Allow about 3–4 hours including transport. Atlanterhavsparken is approximately 3.6 km (2.2 mi) from central Ålesund and is a good choice for families or poor-weather days. The aquarium combines large saltwater displays with outdoor areas for seals and otters.

Local bus number 1 toward Hessa can be used from central Ålesund. Get off at Tuenesvegen and allow another 10–15 minutes on foot. A taxi is simpler when port time is limited; the drive from downtown is normally only several minutes. Check current feeding times and opening arrangements before setting out.

Alnes Lighthouse and Giske

Best treated as a half-day trip. Alnes on Godøya offers open-ocean scenery and a lighthouse visitor centre, while nearby Giske has its medieval church. Reaching the islands involves road travel through the island and tunnel network, so this is less convenient than sightseeing in central Ålesund.

A pre-arranged sightseeing tour is the simplest option for cruise passengers and commonly combines Alnes, Giske and a stop at Mount Aksla. Independent travel is possible with sufficient planning, but check transport connections carefully and leave a larger return margin than for city sightseeing.

Fjord or Coastal Boat Trip

Ålesund is also a practical departure point for boat trips into the surrounding fjords and archipelago. Options can include Hjørundfjord sightseeing or shorter coastal wildlife and RIB trips. These are worthwhile when the sailing fits comfortably inside the ship's port call.

Check the actual departure point and confirmed return time before booking independently. Longer trips toward distant fjord destinations consume a substantial part of the day and are better suited to long port calls or excursions specifically timed for cruise passengers.

Self-Guided Walking Tour

Central Ålesund and Mount Aksla

Difficulty: Moderate. Distance: roughly 4 km (2.5 mi), depending on the berth and small detours. Pure walking time: about 60–75 minutes, plus the 418-step climb. Recommended total time: 2.5–3.5 hours with viewpoints and sightseeing stops.

  1. Cruise terminal exit: Leave the secure quay and follow the signed pedestrian route toward the city centre.
  2. Byparken: Walk to the city park at the foot of Mount Aksla.
  3. Mount Aksla and Fjellstua: Climb the 418 steps, stopping at the intermediate viewpoints before reaching the main panorama over Ålesund, the islands and surrounding mountains.
  4. Kongens gate: Descend the same steps and continue through the central Art Nouveau streets.
  5. Brosundet and Hellebroa: Cross the bridge and pause for the classic view along the narrow harbour channel.
  6. Jugendstilsenteret: See the former pharmacy building and surrounding early-20th-century architecture. Add museum time if your schedule allows.
  7. Molja waterfront: Continue toward the harbour entrance and Molja Lighthouse for another waterside viewpoint.
  8. Return to the ship: Follow the central waterfront back toward the signed cruise-terminal entrance.

The central sections are straightforward, but the Aksla stairs make this route unsuitable for passengers with limited mobility. In wet weather the steps and cobbled streets can be slippery. For an easier version, omit Aksla and concentrate on Brosundet, the Art Nouveau quarter and the waterfront.

Practical Tips

  • Check your ship's exact berth because Ålesund uses several adjacent cruise berths and assignments can change at short notice.
  • Comfortable, slip-resistant footwear is useful for cobbles, slopes and the Aksla stairs.
  • Weather can change quickly; carry a light waterproof layer even when conditions look settled.
  • Use the FRAM app or current local timetable when relying on public buses outside the centre.
  • For independently booked boat trips or drives to the surrounding islands, build in a generous return margin. Central Ålesund is much easier to manage close to departure time.
